messages:
alice.k: quick heads-up — running into a 403 when a system-assigned managed identity in CustomerTenant unwraps an envelope using our Azure Key Vault CMK after they migrated tenants. Anyone hit cross-tenant MI -> AKV unwrap trouble?

ben_ops: what does the error look like from the app / keyvault audit?

alice.k: logs just show `Forbidden` and `client principal does not have key permission unwrapKey` in app logs. Vault is set to use Azure RBAC (data plane). No access policy entries exist.

carol_sec: important note: managed identities are tenant-bound principals. If the MI lives in a different AAD tenant than the vault, AKV won't accept it as a principal unless it's represented in the vault tenant (guest/SP) and granted rights. RBAC vs access policies matters for role name/permissions. Did you grant a Key Vault crypto role?

alice.k: we tried assigning the role `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User` at the vault scope via subscription-level role assignment, but still 403. The principalId used matches the MI's object id from the source tenant.

dave_oncall: two quick checks — firewall/PE and private endpoint configs. If the vault has a private endpoint or only allows selected networks, the request could be blocked earlier and show as auth failure. Also confirm whether the request is actually hitting the expected vault (DNS/alias after migration).

erin_cloud: adding the typical RBAC grant snippet we use for data-plane crypto ops — can try this from the vault's tenant (principal must exist there):

```bash
# grant wrap/unwrap via RBAC (vault tenant)
az role assignment create --assignee <principalObjectIdOrAppId> \n  --role "Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User" \n  --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name>
```

carol_sec: alternate (legacy) path is access policies: if you want to avoid tenant-SP friction, create an access policy on the vault for the principal's object id in the same tenant:

```bash
az keyvault set-policy -n <vault-name> --object-id <principalObjectId> --key-permissions wrapKey unwrapKey get
```

carol_sec: but again — object id must be resolvable in the vault's AAD tenant. For cross-tenant scenarios you have two options: 1) create a service principal (app registration) in the vault tenant and use that identity from the worker, or 2) app/federation patterns (workload identity federation / OIDC) so the external principal can mint tokens in the vault tenant. System-assigned MI alone won't cross tenants.

alice.k: ah — that explains it. The MI is still in the legacy tenant. We'll try creating a service principal in the vault tenant and rotate creds.

ben_ops: for auditing, make sure Key Vault diagnostics are enabled — we push AuditEvent to Log Analytics and an immutable storage account for retention. Example:

```bash
az monitor diagnostic-settings create \n  --resource /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault-name> \n  --name kv-audit --workspace /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/<ws> \n  --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]'
```

ben_ops: that will show principal id, operationName (UnwrapKey), correlation IDs. Useful for triage.

erin_cloud: rotation and emergency rewrap notes: plan to have a secondary key/version and a rewrap workflow. Steps we recommend:
• schedule key rotation (monthly/quarterly depending on policy)
• pre-create a new key version and perform `wrapKey` -> `unwrapKey` test on a sample envelope
• if you must emergency-rotate, rewrap ciphertext with the new key: call the cryptography rewrap/unwrap APIs in sequence or decrypt+re-encrypt with the new key in a short maintenance window.

```python
# pseudo-example using azure-keyvault-keys + CryptographyClient
from azure.keyvault.keys import KeyClient
from azure.keyvault.keys.crypto import CryptographyClient, EncryptionAlgorithm
# get existing key version clients, call rewrap or explicit decrypt/wrap
```

carol_sec: also document a fallback: keep a secondary key in a different vault (or a key version tagged as emergency) and an automated runbook that can re-encrypt data if the primary key becomes unavailable. This gives us an SLA-friendly path.

alice.k: thanks — action items for our team: 1) provision SP in vault tenant & grant `Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User`, 2) enable diag settings to LA + storage, 3) verify Private Endpoint / DNS after migration, 4) add rewrap playbook to runbook repo. I'll post updates.

infra-bot: NOTE: runbook template created: `playbooks/kv-emergency-rewrap.md` (stub). Assigned to alice.k.

dave_oncall: if you need a quick test principal, ping me and I can create a short-lived SP and grant it unwrapKey perms in the vault tenant.

alice.k: will do, thanks all :thumbsup:
